0.heading: Maxwell Engineering Solutions IPO GMP rises to 72% ahead of listing tomorrow
0.intro: Maxwell Engineering Solutions shares are commanding a strong premium in the grey market ahead of their stock market debut on November 6, with the latest grey market premium (GMP) indicating the possibility of substantial listing gains for investors.
0.body:
Maxwell Engineering Solutions shares are commanding a strong premium in the grey market ahead of their stock market debut on November 6, with the latest grey market premium (GMP) indicating the possibility of strong listing gains for investors.

The shares were trading at a GMP of around 71.52 percent on the morning of November 5, according to InvestorGain. At the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 158, this translates into an indicative listing price of around Rs 271 per share.

However, the grey market is an unofficial market, and GMP trends are not a reliable indicator of the actual listing price. The final listing performance will depend on market conditions and investor sentiment on the day of debut.

The Rs 57.64-crore Maxwell Engineering Solutions IPO received an overwhelming response from investors, with the issue subscribed 491.39 times by the end of the three-day bidding period on November 3.

The company's shares are scheduled to list on the NSE Emerge platform on November 6.

The IPO witnessed strong demand across all investor categories, with non-institutional investors (NIIs) leading the subscription tally.

The NII portion was subscribed around 858 times, while the retail investor category saw subscription of approximately 556 times. The qualified institutional buyer (QIB) portion was subscribed 259.4 times.

Investors placed bids for approximately 128.94 crore equity shares against the 26.24 lakh shares on offer during the three-day subscription period from October 30 to November 3.

The issue attracted bids worth approximately Rs 20,372 crore, reflecting strong investor interest in the engineering components manufacturer.

Maxwell Engineering Solutions launched its Rs 57.64-crore IPO through a fresh issue of 36.48 lakh equity shares. The price band was fixed at Rs 150-158 per share.

The Gujarat-based company manufactures precision-engineered components used in underwater pelletising systems.

Check IPO News Here

The company plans to utilise Rs 18 crore from the net IPO proceeds towards purchasing new machinery, laboratory equipment and other utilities for its manufacturing facility.

Another Rs 6.5 crore will be allocated towards the construction of a new office building and manufacturing facility.

Further, Rs 4.3 crore will be used for repayment of outstanding borrowings, while Rs 14 crore has been earmarked for working capital requirements. The remaining proceeds will be utilised for general corporate purposes.

JDA Capital Services is the book-running lead manager to the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.

1.headline: Bombay Coated & Special Steels shares list at 12% premium on BSE — should you buy, sell or hold?
1.heading: Bombay Coated & Special Steels shares list at 12% premium on BSE — should you buy, sell or hold?
1.intro: Bombay Coated & Special Steels shares made a positive debut on the stock exchanges on November 5, listing at a premium of around 12 percent over the company's initial public offering (IPO) price.
1.body:
Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels shares made a positive debut on the stock exchanges on November 5, listing at a premium of around 12 percent over the company's initial public offering (IPO) price.

The shares listed at Rs 92.02 on the NSE, representing a 12.22 percent premium over the IPO price of Rs 82 per share. On the NSE, the stock debuted at Rs 91, reflecting a 10.98 percent premium over the issue price.

Following the listing, Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels' market capitalisation stood at around Rs 578.11 crore.

The listing is in line with the grey market expectation. The GMP had indicated an estimated listing gain of around 10 percent on the morning of November 5, according to Investorgain.

The grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee listing gains. It can fluctuate depending on market conditions and should not be treated as a prediction of the actual listing price.

The Rs 183.06-crore IPO of Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels received a strong response from investors, with the issue subscribed 60.77 times by the close of bidding on November 2, according to exchange data.

The issue received bids for more than 13.5 crore shares against approximately 2.23 crore shares on offer. The non-institutional investor (NII) category led the demand, with its reserved portion subscribed 158.32 times. The qualified institutional buyer (QIB) category was subscribed 35.50 times, while the retail investor portion received 33.73 times subscription.

The IPO opened for subscription on October 29 and closed on November 2. The company had fixed the price band at Rs 78-82 per share.

The minimum lot size was 182 shares, translating into a minimum investment of Rs 14,924 for retail investors at the upper end of the price band.

The IPO was entirely a fresh issue of approximately 2.23 crore equity shares. The company will receive the proceeds from the offering to meet its business requirements.

Of the net proceeds, Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels plans to utilise Rs 125 crore towards the repayment or prepayment of certain borrowings. Another Rs 15.77 crore has been earmarked to finance the acquisition of capital equipment under existing lease arrangements with Siemens Financial Services Private Limited. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

The basis of allotment was scheduled to be finalised on November 3. Refunds for unsuccessful applicants and credit of allotted shares to demat accounts are scheduled for November 4, ahead of the listing.

Smart Horizon Capital Advisors is the book-running lead manager to the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.

Should you buy, sell or hold?

Sarvam Goel, founder of Pocketful said, "Given the healthy demand across categories and supportive tailwinds from rising steel consumption and greater outsourcing of processing."

"Allottees can consider booking partial profits on listing and holding the rest with a long-term view," he added.

Another analyst, Mahesh M. Ojha, Vice President Research &amp; Business Development at Kantilal Chhaganlal Securities Pvt. Ltd. said, "Investors who have received allotment may consider booking partial profits on listing and holding the remaining shares for the long term, considering the company's business positioning, growth opportunities and debt reduction plans."

About Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels

Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels is a steel processing company that converts steel coils into processed steel products through operations such as slitting, cut-to-length processing, shearing and embossing.

Its products cater to industrial customers that require processed steel for their manufacturing operations. The company's manufacturing facilities are located in Wada and Bhiwandi in Maharashtra, Ghiloth in Rajasthan, and Sri City in Andhra Pradesh.

2.headline: SEBI sets up panel to revive dormant startup listing platform
2.heading: SEBI sets up panel to revive dormant startup listing platform
2.intro: The platform was introduced in 2014 to give startups and new-age companies access to public capital markets before they meet the eligibility norms for the main board
2.body:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Wednesday formed a working group to review the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP), a listing route for startups that has drawn few takers more than a decade after its launch.

The platform was introduced in 2014 to give startups and new-age companies access to public capital markets before they meet the eligibility norms for the main board. It has seen little activity since.

The panel will assess whether the current framework is still relevant and effective in helping innovation-led companies raise capital, without diluting investor protection. Its scope covers research-stage, pre-revenue, intellectual property-led and deep-tech firms, along with other technology-intensive businesses.

The working group will examine listing and fundraising rules, investor eligibility criteria, post-listing obligations and the process for migrating companies from the IGP to the main board.

The review comes as India’s startup ecosystem pushes into biotechnology, semiconductors and space. Companies in these sectors typically have longer development cycles and funding needs that differ from those of mature businesses, making conventional listing norms a poor fit.
